description.from:
Required packet-and-layer report fields.

Per layer: evaluable positives, **reachable** positives, matched positives, exact-concept recall, ancestor-category recall where applicable, classification accuracy, strict correct-label recall, precision, unread count and rate, distinct evidence-file coverage, ineligible counts by reason, unscorable findings, and gate exceptions.

Totals are denominator-weighted within a layer only; no scalar mixes heterogeneous layers.

Two coverage views are both required, because repeated annotations in one file distort a case-only unread rate — discourse alone carries 288 annotations across far fewer files.

A language/capability slice accompanies the full report and is the load-bearing view: 960 of 1,792 annotations sit on extensions ingest cannot open, so without the slice, results on supported inputs are hidden rather than merely diluted.
description.to:
Required packet-and-layer report fields.

Per layer: accepted canonical positives; evaluable positives; matched positives; exact-concept recall over the full accepted/evaluable denominator; ancestor-category recall where applicable; classification accuracy; strict correct-label recall; precision plus explicit computability state; unread count/rate; distinct evidence-file coverage; entity partial-coverage counts; ineligible counts by reason; unscorable findings; migration-readiness blockers; and gate exceptions.

Capability support is diagnostic only: report `declaredCapabilitySupported` counts and `declaredCapabilityCoverage`, tied to the scanner and adapter-map digest. Never print recall over that subset as the headline and never remove unsupported canonical concepts from raw recall.

Legacy source-token-only or unresolved endpoint rows are migration-incomplete, not accepted canonical positives. Report them in readiness accounting by review state and reason.

Totals are denominator-weighted within a layer only; no scalar mixes heterogeneous layers. Both annotation/entity-weighted and distinct-file coverage are required. A language/capability slice accompanies the full scorecard without replacing it.
